claims.disproof_condition: Revisit if NVIDIA's partner list changes materially in later CPO generations (companies added/dropped), or if detachable-fiber architecture is replaced (e.g., fully sealed fiber, removing the connector layer's value).
claims.statement: NVIDIA's CPO switch stack has two layers previously absent from this graph, both with customer-side (NVIDIA) role attribution: (a) fiber attach — optical connectors and fiber assemblies linking front-panel ELS via polarization-maintaining fiber into the silicon photonics engine; named experts (blog header): Browave, Corning, Senko, TFC Communication, Coherent — Browave (3163.TW) and TFC Communication (300394.SZ) are listed pure-plays and onboard candidates pending four-dimension screening; (b) CPO packaging/assembly — SPIL packages the NVIDIA CPO multi-chip module (wafer bumping, sort, assembly, test); Foxconn and Fabrinet do system-level CPO assembly and chassis integration. SENKO is private; SPIL is an OSAT (ASE group per background, unverified here).

claims.disproof_condition: Lower substitutability if NVIDIA names a second silicon photonics foundry (e.g., GlobalFoundries) for a shipping CPO product; raise only with evidence competitors failed qualification.
claims.statement: TSMC's COUPE process (EIC+PIC integration via 3D chip-on-wafer stacking) is the named silicon photonics engine process for NVIDIA's CPO switches. Substitutability judged 4/5 for this relation: customer-side naming by NVIDIA plus no other foundry named in the ecosystem; not 5 because merchant silicon photonics foundries exist (unnamed here) and NVIDIA could dual-source future generations.

sources.quote: The TSMC silicon photonics Compact Universal Photonic Engine (COUPE) process integrates electronic integrated circuits (EIC) with silicon photonic integrated circuits (PIC) using the 3D chip-on-wafer and chip-stacking packaging technologies.
SPIL is well-known for packaging complex integrated assemblies including wafer bumping, wafer sort, assembly, and testing for the NVIDIA CPO multi-chip module.
